set.st: Heinrich Maas of Cooperstown left a will that disposed of a pot of gold he had buried; its place was written on a slip of paper kept in his watch case. When the estate looked, the hole the pot had sat in was found, but the gold was gone. Estate attorneys Schenian & Kelley cited William Maas before Judge Anderson on 21 Mar 1898 'to tell what he knows about the gold'; no outcome was reported in 1898-99. The Two Rivers Chronicle of 22 February 1898 confirms the sum at $1,500 in gold and says the pot had disappeared from its hiding place. Pin is approximate (town or township only), not the spot itself.
set.v: A buried pot of about $1,500 in gold named in his will (gone from its hole when the estate looked)
set.tovw: Lead grade D: hole found empty in 1898, the $1,500 pot gone, probably taken by family; the March hearing's outcome was never reported
